push.body:
Perfect Game #15, PhogsToffees. A 10.0 against Chudz UTD. If football had a dictionary, your picture would be next to 'flawless'.

THE GOOD
+ A perfect 10.0, your 15th Perfect Game for us. Bottle that and bring it next match.
+ Shots 7, up from your usual 2. Small wins add up to big ones.
+ Man of the Match, your 30th for us. Leaders make the hard moments look easy.
+ Match rating 10.0, up from your usual 7.4. That's the version of you I'm building the team around.
+ Part of a 4-1 beating of Chudz UTD. Put that in the team scrapbook.

THE BAD
- 64% passing (9 of 14, down from your usual 77%). From the clipboard: If you're pressed from behind, play it back the way you're facing. Don't turn into trouble.
- 4 of 7 shots on target. A little secret: Shoot from central, inside the box. Tight angles and long range are where shots go wide. Steady does it.
- Both you and BellyTb1 dipped on shot selection. Lean on each other: cut it back to each other.
- Key passes 0, down from your usual 2. Back to basics: Arrive late at the edge of the box for cutbacks. That's where midfield chances come from.
- 1 tackle won: -0.1. Easy fix, big payoff.

Practice this: With your back to goal, shield it and set it back to the runner facing play. Turning into traffic is a coin flip.

PhogsToffees, write this on your hand if you have to: Every game is a teacher. Some just grade harder.

You make coaching fun. - Coach Lasso

Mercy me, Soup_Kitchen22. A 7.5. That one goes in the scrapbook, page one.

+ 6 tackles attempted (up from your usual 3). You got stuck in like a boot in Missouri mud.
+ 1 key pass. You're the opener on the team's toolbelt.

+ 7.5: your 2nd best match performance of the season. Remember how that felt.

THE BAD

- on-ball involvement is your shared homework with tuxedo_slide: make triangles, 1-2 touch.
- Missed tackles 4, up from your usual 2. That needs to look different next time out.
- None of the team's 10 shots. Let's try: When you've got a clear look inside the box, pull the trigger. Hesitation lets defenders recover.

Session plan: Drift into the half-space between their midfield and defense. It's the hardest spot to mark.

Soup_Kitchen22, my granddaddy told me this and now I'm telling you: Taking on a challenge is a lot like riding a horse. Comfortable is overrated.

Go put your feet up. - Coach Lasso

push.body:
A 7.3 against Chudz UTD, tuxedo_slide. Your 4th best match performance of the season, and it felt like it.

THE GOOD
+ 1 key pass. Your passes had GPS and good manners.
+ Keep finding PhogsToffees; it's working like a charm.
+ Giveaways 4, down from your usual 8. Proof you've got another gear.
+ Better match rating than any of their humans (7.3 vs their best 7.0). Pure hustle, and hustle is free.

THE BAD
- Only 14 passes. My two cents: Give the passer an angle - diagonal to the ball, not flat in a line where it can't reach you. Trust me on that one.
- Only 2 tackles attempted. Try this: When the ball is lost, the nearest player presses and everyone else closes the passing lanes. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast.
- Red card. One more thing: No slide tackles from behind or as the last defender. A red card costs us the whole match.
- Soup_Kitchen22 had the same on-ball involvement trouble. Team up on it: make triangles, 1-2 touch.
- Shots 0, down from your usual 2. Small change, big gain: Attack the box. Near post and far post on every cross and every cutback.

THE UGLY
! Red card: the team played a player down for the rest of it. That's below the line we drew together, and the line is the line. Fundamentals: If you're beaten, sprint the recovery run goal-side instead of reaching in.

Backyard drill: Play with your head up between touches. You can't find a pass you never looked for.

tuxedo_slide, take this with you: Nobody remembers the miss. Everybody remembers the response.

I'll be smiling about that one all week. - Coach Lasso
